title: Files, folders & cloud sync
blurb: OneDrive, iCloud, Dropbox, lost or deleted files, search, file types.

remedies.title: I deleted a file by mistake
remedies.why: Deleted files usually go to the Recycle Bin / Bin first, and cloud services keep deleted files for weeks.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+Z (⌘Z) straight away in the same folder to undo the delete.
Open the Recycle Bin (Bin on Mac), right-click the file › Restore (Put Back).
OneDrive / SharePoint: onedrive.com › Recycle bin (kept 30–93 days). iCloud: iCloud.com › Drive › Recently Deleted. Google Drive and Dropbox have their own Trash.
File History or a previous version: right-click the folder › Restore previous versions.
Time Machine: open the folder in Finder, then Time Machine in the menu bar › Browse Time Machine Backups.

remedies.escalate: For files on a work shared drive, IT can usually restore from the server's backup; tell them the path and when it was last there.

remedies.title: OneDrive isn't syncing
remedies.why: Sync is paused, you're signed out, a file name or size isn't allowed, the disk or OneDrive storage is full, or OneDrive's own data got stuck.

steps.text: Click the OneDrive cloud icon: resume if paused, and read any error it shows.
Check you're signed in and have storage left (OneDrive › Settings › Account).
Rename files with characters OneDrive doesn't accept (" * : < > ? / \ |) or very long paths.
Quit OneDrive and start it again.
Reset OneDrive (re-syncs everything; your files stay).
Reset OneDrive: quit it, then run the ResetOneDriveApp command inside the app (OneDrive.app › Show Package Contents › Contents › Resources).

remedies.escalate: Give IT the error text from the OneDrive icon.

remedies.title: OneDrive files show a cloud icon or take space I don't have
remedies.why: Files On-Demand keeps files online until you open them (cloud icon) or keeps them on the computer (green tick).

steps.text: Right-click a folder › Free up space to keep it online only; Always keep on this device to keep it offline.
Turn on Storage Sense to free space on files you haven't opened in a while.
Online-only files need internet to open; mark folders you use offline (travel) as Always keep.

remedies.title: Duplicate files with my computer's name in them
remedies.why: The same file changed in two places before syncing, so the sync service kept both.

steps.text: Open both copies, keep the right one, delete the other.
Close files on other devices before editing; work in Office's co-authoring for shared files.
Avoid editing the same file offline on two computers.

remedies.title: iCloud Drive isn't syncing
remedies.why: iCloud storage is full, you're signed out, low power mode pauses it, or a big upload is still going.

steps.text: Check iCloud storage isn't full (System Settings › your name › iCloud).
Turn off Low Power Mode; it pauses iCloud uploads.
In Finder's sidebar, the progress circle next to iCloud Drive shows what's uploading; give big uploads time.
Open iCloud for Windows and check iCloud Drive is ticked and you're signed in; restart the computer.
Sign out of iCloud and back in as a last resort (keep a copy of files first).

remedies.title: Can't open a file: "How do you want to open this file?"
symptoms: how do you want to open this
remedies.why: No app on this computer opens that file type, or the wrong one is set as default.

steps.text: Show file extensions to see the real type: File Explorer › View › Show › File name extensions.
Choose an app: right-click › Open with › choose another app, and tick Always.
Set the default per type: Settings › Apps › Default apps › search the extension.
Right-click › Get Info › Open with › choose the app › Change All.
Look up the extension (e.g. .heic, .pages, .msg) to find the right app; many open in a browser or online viewer.

remedies.title: iPhone photos (.HEIC) won't open
symptoms: photos from iphone won't open on pc
remedies.why: iPhones save photos as HEIC, which Windows needs an extension to open and many websites don't accept.

steps.text: Install "HEIF Image Extensions" from the Microsoft Store (free).
On the iPhone: Settings › Camera › Formats › Most Compatible saves JPEG instead; Photos › Transfer to Mac or PC › Automatic converts when copying.
On a Mac, open the photo in Preview › File › Export › JPEG.

remedies.title: Open or make a ZIP file
remedies.why: ZIP files bundle many files into one; both systems handle ZIP themselves.

steps.text: Open: right-click › Extract All. Make: select files › right-click › Compress to ZIP file. Windows 11 also opens .rar and .7z.
Open: double-click the ZIP. Make: select files › right-click › Compress.
Extract files before working on them; editing inside a ZIP doesn't save back.

remedies.title: Windows search finds nothing or is slow
remedies.why: The search index is incomplete or damaged, or the folder isn't indexed.

steps.text: Rebuild the search index (takes a while to fill in again).
Choose Enhanced (whole PC) or add folders: Settings › Privacy & security › Searching Windows.
If the Start menu search box itself doesn't respond, restart Explorer.

remedies.title: Spotlight search finds nothing
remedies.why: Spotlight's index is incomplete or the folder is excluded.

steps.text: Check the categories you want are on, and the folder isn't in Spotlight Privacy.
Rebuild the index: add the disk to Spotlight Privacy, wait a moment, then remove it; Spotlight re-indexes (can take hours).

remedies.title: "Access denied" or "You don't have permission" on a file or folder
remedies.why: The file belongs to another user, it's on a protected system folder, or a shared folder's permissions don't include you.

steps.text: Save your own files in Documents, Desktop or OneDrive, not in system folders.
For a file from an old computer or another user, copy it into your Documents folder.
A Mac app may need "Files and Folders" or "Full Disk Access" permission.
Controlled folder access in Windows Security can block apps from Documents; allow the app there.

remedies.escalate: For shared work folders, IT has to give you access; tell them the folder path.

remedies.title: "File name too long" or path too long when copying
remedies.why: Many Windows apps still have a 260-character limit on the full path of a file.

steps.text: Shorten folder names along the path, or move the folder closer to the drive's top (e.g. C:\Work).
Zip the folder before copying it, then extract it somewhere with a shorter path.
